rows.title: Governor, Democrats unveil 10-year plan to prevent Coloradans’ property taxes from rising too quickly
rows.standfirst: The proposal hinges on voter approval of a measure on the November ballot. If the plan fails, the average Colorado homeowner would experience a property tax increase of 40%.

rows.title: House Democrats will try to resurrect provisions in Colorado land-use bill that were gutted in the Senate
rows.standfirst: The House sponsors of Senate Bill 213 want to add back provisions mandating density. If approved, the measure could lead to a clash with the Senate in the final days of the 2023 lawmaking term

rows.title: Four Colorado colleges granted $5M by Delta Dental to expand oral health programs
rows.standfirst: The grants from Delta Dental of Colorado Foundation will either expand existing dental hygiene programs or create new ones to address a workforce shortage

rows.title: This Grand Junction company makes the “world’s best sleeping bags” — but you won’t find them in stores
rows.standfirst: As more businesses look for success in Colorado’s Grand Valley, Wiggy’s remains one of the mainstays of the region’s growing outdoor recreation industry

rows.title: Cinco de Mayo has been distorted into a day of drinking. Denver groups are reclaiming the holiday’s true meaning.
rows.standfirst: Several leaders in Denver’s Westwood community are fighting back against the so-called “Cinco De Drinko” culture

rows.title: Can a mixed-income community transform Denver’s Sun Valley neighborhood?
rows.standfirst: An ambitious plan to revitalize one of Denver’s poorest neighborhoods displaced 1,000 people. Fewer than 20% have returned as rebuilding drags on.

rows.title: Use our calculator to determine what your new property tax bill would be under the Colorado legislature’s relief plan
rows.standfirst: The median increase in home values across the state was 40% since June 2020, causing a spike in property tax bills

rows.title: Two programs that kept Coloradans fed through the pandemic are shrinking. One may even shut down.
rows.standfirst: Food justice programs are scrambling to keep delivering fresh fruits and vegetables to people in need.

rows.title: Colorado may have its best boating season in over a decade thanks to this winter’s large snowfall
rows.standfirst: But if the deep snow melts too fast, the rafting season that might have been could end in a rush of dangerous water and debris.

rows.title: How first-time buyers are finding success — and frustration — in Colorado’s housing market
rows.standfirst: Higher interest rates and for-sale prices may be a barrier, but for those ready to plunge into home ownership, the best advice is to get educated.

rows.title: What’s Working: The back and forth recession fears continue in Colorado’s economy
rows.standfirst: Yes, no and maybe but what’s it to you? Plus: The $1 fee to file a new business startup expected to end this month, first-time homebuyers do exist and more

rows.title: In major last-minute course correction, Colorado Democrats move to issue $2 billion in flat-rate taxpayer refund checks
rows.standfirst: Single filers would get $650 under the proposed change, while joint filers would get $1,300. The proposal hinges on a separate property tax relief ballot measure passing in November.

rows.title: How a Colorado college is using rapid rehousing to help its students experiencing homelessness
rows.standfirst: Fort Lewis College’s first-in-state program served 108 students in its inaugural year.

rows.title: Boulder company puts steelmaking on a greenhouse gas diet with low-carbon iron
rows.standfirst: Electra is patenting a low-temperature iron-making method that can also clean up discarded ore piles, with backing of Colorado congressional delegation.

rows.title: Civitas pauses fight to tap oil and gas under Boulder County open space, as battle looms for land near Aurora Reservoir
rows.standfirst: The 5-year court battle over mineral leases under 552 acres south of Longmont ended with one of Colorado’s biggest producers putting the Blue Paintbrush project on hold indefinitely

rows.title: A decade after marijuana legalization, Grand Junction finally has rules for recreational cannabis sales
rows.standfirst: Would-be sellers of weed say they lost millions in the 2 years it took the Mesa County city to create rules for issuing 10 retail licenses

rows.title: Colorado legislature runs out of time on just-cause eviction bill, single-payer health care study
rows.standfirst: At least four bills died on the calendar Sunday after the Colorado legislature ran out of time to debate them before the 2023 lawmaking term ends Monday

rows.title: Colorado Senate kills languishing land-use bill from Jared Polis that aimed to boost affordable housing
rows.standfirst: The chamber will not take up the measure, Senate Bill 213, before the lawmaking term ends at 11:59 p.m., effectively shelving the legislation

rows.title: Colorado legislature asks voters to approve 10-year property tax relief plan, make $2B in taxpayer refund checks equal
rows.standfirst: The Colorado General Assembly ended its 120-day lawmaking term Monday night by putting a measure on the November ballot

rows.title: Why was your utility bill so high this past winter? Blame the drought — and California.
rows.standfirst: As the drought cut California’s hydropower production, the utilities in state scrambled to buy natural gas, driving up costs across the West

rows.title: A newly approved boat-in campground hopes to make rafting the Colorado River more accessible
rows.standfirst: Kampa Lampa Campground is set to open in early August. Owner Kathy Haas says marketing will be “no problem.”

rows.title: What’s Working: Front Range rents were mostly flat in April. Here’s how they’ve changed over four years.
rows.standfirst: Fort Collins and Colorado Springs metro areas outpaced the Denver metro for rent hikes since 2019. Plus: Median home prices fell last month but not enough for many renters.

rows.title: After decades of closures, a new 40-bed psych unit in Aurora may represent a U-turn in mental health care
rows.standfirst: The state-of-the-art unit will open this summer at UCHealth University of Colorado Hospital, alleviating crowded emergency rooms filled with people in mental health crisis

rows.title: Colorado offers millions in grants to help government, business truck and car fleets go electric
rows.standfirst: Clean electrification mandates for big trucks come at a big cost, and new grants can defray company expenses

rows.title: A program in Gunnison is providing fresh, local food to teachers — for free
rows.standfirst: Easing one source of stress for preschool educators could make teachers better in the classroom, managers of the collaborative food program say

rows.title: Census: Colorado’s smaller communities are growing while large cities level off
rows.standfirst: Keenesburg grew by 65% from 2020 to 2022, estimates show. Large cities were relatively stable while some ski towns lost residents.

rows.title: Residents who sued claiming squalid conditions ask judge to let them represent everyone in their apartment complex
rows.standfirst: Four Mint Urban Infinity residents want class-action status for their lawsuit so people living in any of the 550 apartments can be compensated for problems that went on for years

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s April job growth is the best in 12 months, but it’s slower than the nation’s
rows.standfirst: The state’s unemployment rate was unchanged at 2.8%. Plus: Wages are up, unless you add in inflation, Denver renters see more perks, and more!

rows.title: Venezuelan migrants share stories of their dangerous monthslong journey to Denver
rows.standfirst: They saw bodies — including those of children. Some were assaulted on a train, others were kidnapped. They risked run-ins with mafias and corrupt cops.

rows.title: Chevron’s $7.6B purchase of PDC Energy creates the biggest oil and gas company in Colorado
rows.standfirst: Denver-based PDC Energy’s share price sagged under concerns over increased regulation, but the company has received 1,000 drilling permits in the last 10 months

rows.title: Colorado repealed law limiting municipal internet, making it easier for towns to build their own
rows.standfirst: More than 160 cities, towns and counties opted out of Senate Bill 152, and some built their own gigabit service that was 4,000 times faster. But there were other reasons for the repeal.

rows.title: Broomfield closing 16-year-old 1stBank Center, plans to knock it down by next spring
rows.standfirst: Built to jump-start development at the city’s edge, 1stBank Center is heavily in debt and siphoning cash from other urban renewal zones to pay its bills

rows.title: Air controller staffing shortages add to potential travel delays as summer season starts
rows.standfirst: Airline travelers expected to exceed pre-pandemic levels this weekend in Denver, so it’s best to plan ahead for multiple reasons.

rows.title: One year after Aurora’s $2M camping ban, it’s unclear if the ordinance is successful
rows.standfirst: City leaders said they’re working to hire more staff to enforce the ban, to improve data tracking and to find more permanent housing solutions

rows.title: PHOTOS: After weeks of bombing and scraping, Colorado’s mountain roads are ready for summer traffic
rows.standfirst: Several connector roads are opening just in time for Memorial Day traffic

rows.title: No, we don’t know when Casa Bonita will open. But we do know what it’ll look like — mostly.
rows.standfirst: The iconic restaurant offered a no-questions-allowed behind-the-scenes tour of its remodel

rows.title: Crested Butte Mountain Resort lift mechanics unanimously vote to form union
rows.standfirst: The lift maintenance crew at the Vail Resorts-owned ski area in Mount Crested Butte is the second in the nation to unionize and part of a growing labor movement in the resort industry

rows.title: What’s Working: Welcome to summer 2023 travel season, as airlines and labor issues collide
rows.standfirst: Pilots are picketing, airlines are hiring. What that means for summer travel. Plus: Colorado and the debt ceiling, job complications, more!

rows.title: “A season to celebrate” as U.S., Rocky Mountain ski areas experience record visitation
rows.standfirst: Record snowfall draws highest-ever visits to Rocky Mountain ski areas and an all-time high of 67.4 million skier visits to U.S. ski resorts

rows.title: Colorado’s mountain towns are being loved to death. A new roadmap can help them escape the “amenity trap.”
rows.standfirst: A new report by Headwaters Economics highlights progressive growth strategies across the country to help amenity-rich communities navigate growth challenges

rows.title: From the back of a van to a $1.9 million facility, adaptive sports have become core to Colorado skiing
rows.standfirst: Ignite Adaptive Sports and Eldora ski area are partnering on a new 12,000-square-foot, multi-million-dollar building set to open in 2024.

rows.title: Xcel Energy makes money building power plants. The more it builds the more consumers have to pay — with no end in sight.
rows.standfirst: While the strategy delivers returns to investors, a cascade of rate increases could lead to “a public backlash” a credit agency warns.
